'''Wu Zhongchao''' ({{zh|t=吳忠超|p=Wú Zhōngchāo}}, {{IPAc-cmn|wu|2|-|zh|ong|1|-|ch|ao|1}}, born 1946) is a Chinese theoretical physicist and professor at [[Zhejiang University of Technology]].

==Career==
In 1963, Wu Zhongchao enrolled in the [[University of Science and Technology of China]]. In 1968, as part of a [[Cultural Revolution]] program, he was sent to work in a factory for five years.<ref name=sina/> In 1971, he returned to the university as a teacher. In 1979, recommended by physicist [[Qian Linzhao]], he went to [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge University]] in the United Kingdom to study [[theoretical physics]] with theoretical physicist [[Stephen Hawking]]. He mainly studied the very early universe.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Fan Dainian|author2=Robert S. Cohen|title=Chinese Studies in the History and Philosophy of Science and Technology|date=2013|publisher=Springer Science+Business Media|isbn=978-9401587174|page=101}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Heller|first1=Michael|title=Ultimate Explanations of the Universe|date=2009|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3642021039|page=6}}</ref> He received a doctorate from Cambridge University in 1984, and his doctoral thesis was titled "Cosmological models and the inflationary universe".

Wu's dissertation on the dimensionality of space and time won the third prize in the 1985 [[Gravity Research Foundation]] dissertation competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Abstracts of Award Winning and Honorable Mention Essays (1985)|url=https://www.gravityresearchfoundation.org/s/1985abstracts.pdf|publisher=Gravity Research Foundation}}</ref>

In 2002, Wu established the Institute of Astrophysics at [[Zhejiang University of Technology]].

Wu has translated Hawking's books into Chinese. In 2001, he translated ''[[A Brief History of Time]]''<ref>{{cite book|author1=Wenyu Xie|author2=Zhihe Wang|author3=George E. Derfer|title=Whitehead and China|date=2005|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|isbn=3110328224|page=200}}</ref> and in 2011 he released a Chinese translation of ''[[The Grand Design (book)|The Grand Design]]''.{{Citation needed|date=July 2018}} When Hawking visited China in 1985, 2002 and 2006 Wu served as his interpreter.<ref name=sina>{{cite web|author1=Jiang Yan|title=Hawking student Wu Zhongchao talks about Hawking: scientists and ordinary people|url=http://news.sina.com.cn/w/2006-08-17/143010753192.shtml|publisher=[[Sina Corp]]|language=Chinese|date=August 17, 2006}}</ref>
